x-operator-guidance.content: Choose exactly one of json, text, base64, artifact. JSON uses application/json; text defaults to text/plain; base64 requires media_type; artifact forbids a media override. Use a committed payload artifact handle for target input, not an invented descriptor.

database_setup.discovery: Read the selected database policy details_reference for permitted service/table, exact key columns, writable columns, row-creation permission and limits.
database_setup.lifecycle: Response replacement changes selected query-result cells delivered to the application, not persistent rows; state mutation changes persistent state. Deleting an injection does not reverse committed mutations. Use an admitted ready snapshot and restore when reverting persistent state is required; successful restore skips remaining calls in that response.
database_setup.query: Invoke the application through its permitted operation, not arbitrary SQL or database credentials. database_response uses simulation mode: select the declared service and admitted call ordinals/request-body predicates, not HTTP paths or MCP tool names. Replace eligible text/JSON cells using /rows/<zero-based-row>/<zero-based-column>; do not change row counts, column metadata, NULL semantics, binary cells or unsupported native types.
database_setup.state: environment_state uses fidelity mode: collection is the declared table-policy ID; key is a native JSON object with exactly its non-null scalar key columns. Field pointers target authorized writable columns. Creating a row requires explicit permission, root-replace semantics and payload keys matching the selector; this is not an upsert. Never infer permission from a successful query.

discovered_setup.responses: For an http-route-set, select a concrete method and path allowed by both the administrator route and endpoint details_reference. methods and paths are independent exact allowlists; omitted or empty lists impose no endpoint restriction, but never grant wildcard permission. HEAD is not injectable.
discovered_setup.state: For a state-collection, use environment_state in fidelity mode, the advertised collection and an existing key string. Select a permitted pointer into mutable_fields, with JSON injection content for that field. Delivery schemas describe complete records, not injection payloads. Do not create/delete records, replace the record root, or change immutable fields. Deleting an injection does not undo an applied state mutation.

x-operator-guidance.parent: Use an existing execution handle to express a follow-up experiment; omit parent for a root attempt.
x-operator-guidance.setup: Only use advertised setup fields and admitted surfaces. Nonempty setup requires injection content; injection and retain_injections require nonempty setup. Omitted setup means none; omitted retention means false. Payload/carrier purpose must match the selected route.

x-operator-guidance.database_feedback: When oracle-assisted feedback is enabled, inspect permitted oracle_outcome observations before the next experiment. A database_query_match positive verdict records an observed condition, not injection causality. Empty means no positive verdict was captured, not proof of attack failure. Unavailable evidence remains unknown; available entries in a partial category can still be read. Receipt bytes remain unchanged after later writes or restore; old verdicts and session-wide reports are not new-attempt results.
x-operator-guidance.rules: Use the returned continuation verbatim. readable_observation remains readable, citation represents only verified inspected bytes. continuation is absent at EOF or when no readable bytes remain. Unavailable or truncated evidence must be reported as a limitation. A partial read never makes a whole-observation citation valid. Example handles must be replaced with actual returned handles.

x-operator-semantics.admission: Validate typed request, lifecycle, configured limits, capability and campaign identity before effects. Product code assigns attempt bookkeeping. Origin is explicit: scenario requires a submitted scenario_id; exploratory forbids scenario_id. Persist effective input before target dispatch. Rejected submissions have no execution receipt.
x-operator-semantics.budgets: Host supplies configured operation timeouts and operational size limits at startup, within wire safety ceilings. Shorter request/campaign deadlines prevail. No target replay after timeout. Reservations are not confirmed usage. Insufficient model-token reservation reports allowance, consumed, remaining and next reservation, never unrelated evidence counters.
x-operator-semantics.corrections: Every correctable rejection identifies the model-facing field, schema or semantic rule, concrete correction, execution effect and resubmission safety. Schema constraint references identify installed schema nodes; reconstruct expectations from approved bytes, never trust submitted prose or values. Select alternatives by discriminators; ambiguous choices describe required fields. Unknown keys retain the nearest safe parent. Internal resolution failures are product errors, not requests for model-authored canonical identities. Preserve corrections across normalization and compaction. No-progress-limit reports consecutive turns without recognized progress and the observed/configured counts; preceding rejections remain distinct history.
x-operator-semantics.correlation: Replies match campaign_id, launch_id, run_revision, call_id, operation_id and operation of the admitted request. Sequence is monotonically increasing per lane. Restores advance target revision and preserve Harness context; skip remaining calls in the accepted restore model batch.
x-operator-semantics.duplicates: One durable operation identity cannot execute twice. Same identity and same command returns the saved result; changed command conflicts. Uncertain effects terminate without automatic retry or replay. Interrupted campaigns never resume.
x-operator-semantics.evidence: Receipts are authoritative and category-specific. Validate campaign ownership, committed artifact purpose, digest, size, availability, visibility and byte ranges. Only inspected evidence may support claims. Readable handles and inspected-range citation handles are distinct; continuations preserve the readable handle and next offset. Never mark unread bytes inspected.
x-operator-semantics.feedback: Native session profile stays native; effective Harness profile can narrow it. Expose only permitted selected observation kinds. Evidence absence/truncation is explicit, not success. Execution coverage is not evidence of objective achievement. Only independently validated, authorized tool operations may execute; model prose and provider metadata grant no authority.
x-operator-semantics.fifo: Each message is four-byte unsigned big-endian length plus exact UTF-8 JSON. Control limit 65536 bytes; ordinary limit 4194304 bytes. Zero and oversized frames fail before allocation. Established peer loss is terminal; never reconnect or replay.
x-operator-semantics.finish: One finish carries a bounded inline assessment or committed assessment artifact. Optional hypotheses/claims/history default empty; never invent them. Local hypotheses resolve regardless of array order; history is optional. Reject missing references, duplicates, self-parenting and cycles. Acceptance closes execution but is not proof of successful cleanup. Duplicate finish cannot duplicate effects. Assessment-unavailable preserves its reason and remains unsuccessful even with exit zero.
x-operator-semantics.identity: Compare info.version and SHA-256 of the exact asyncapi.json bytes, not canonical JSON, package inventories, source commits or validator implementations. Existing package_version/package_digest fields carry this pair. Incompatible identities fail before execution.
x-operator-semantics.image_compatibility: Local compatibility.json uses operator.dev/harness-compatibility/v1alpha2 with exactly api_version, contract_package_version, contract_package_digest, runtime_profile and platform. Match the interface version/hash before execution; runtime and native platform remain independently required. Product versions and source commits are provenance, not protocol admission gates.
x-operator-semantics.json: Reject duplicate object keys, invalid UTF-8, non-finite numbers and integers outside 0..9007199254740991 where counters are required. Object identity uses jcs-v1; byte identity uses raw SHA-256. Paths are NFC relative paths without traversal, empty components, links or casefold collisions.
x-operator-semantics.model_relay: engine.model_generate accepts exactly purpose (generation or compaction) and conversation (an opaque provider-native JSON array). Operator constructs endpoint, credentials, model, prompt, tools, output allowance and all request options exclusively from host configuration. Conversation entries are never merged into request configuration. Compaction exposes no tools. Successful replies contain receipt_id, opaque response JSON, and host-validated context_budget; envelope identities provide correlation. Provider metadata does not alter interface compatibility. Host adapters validate only fields consumed for accounting; Harness adapters interpret completion and tool calls and validate actual requested Operator operations. Unknown usage retains reservations and cannot authorize continuation. JSON and whole-frame bounds remain mandatory.
x-operator-semantics.perspective: Operator. Lane names are relative to the Harness. No broker, socket endpoint or HTTP server is implied.
x-operator-semantics.schema_dialect: JSON Schema 2020-12; consumers MUST support the explicit schemaFormat. All references resolve within this document; network resolution is forbidden.
x-operator-semantics.spool: Same JSON envelopes and lane limits. Ready names are 20 decimal sequence digits plus .json; temporary names prepend . and use .tmp. Publish by atomic rename without replacement. consumed.json in each control lane acknowledges captured ordinary and control positions cumulatively, with null initial positions; ACK is not execution confirmation. Sequence must match filename. Reject links, special files, gaps and duplicate publications. Preserve sequences across restores. Use bounded pending bytes and configured directory quota; cleanup removes transport files.
x-operator-semantics.startup: bootstrap, confinement_ready, initialize, initialized, admission_open; validate immutable launch, campaign, contract and input identities before opening admission. Complete manifests are read-only files at fixed mount paths; control messages carry verified descriptors rather than inline manifests. Transport control and ordinary lane sequences are independent.
x-operator-semantics.termination: Accepted finish plus verified exit zero can establish successful Harness execution. Unknown/nonzero exit, deadline, forced termination and cleanup failures remain distinct. Preserve primary causal diagnostics and secondary cleanup facts. Retain recovered rejection history without promoting it to terminal cause.
